entities.name: SoftBank Group
entities.desc: Japan's #1 company by market cap as of June 2026 (¥47.2T, +73% YTD), displacing Toyota. ARM Holdings (~90% stake) accounts for ~60% of NAV. Sovereign AI cloud platform for Japanese government and regulated institutions — NVIDIA H100 clusters in Tokyo & Osaka. Lead sponsor of Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (30+ firm consortium, ¥1T NEDO backing). **SB OAI Japan GK (Issue #18, Jun 2026):** SoftBank-OpenAI JV launched 'Patching as a Service' — AI-powered enterprise vulnerability assessment and remediation for Japan's top 3,000 companies, starting with critical infrastructure (airports, power grids, transit). 50 security specialists at launch; target 1,000 personnel. Son Masayoshi framed AI-powered cyberattacks as a 'Black Ships' (黒船) moment — national crisis framing positions SoftBank for METI government procurement contracts. First revenue signal expected August 2026 earnings.

entities.name: NEC Corporation
entities.desc: Japan's largest system integrator. Anthropic's first Japan-based Global Partner; deploying Claude Opus across ~30,000 NEC Group engineers via BluStellar Scenario platform. Member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (10%+ equity). Runs dual-stack hedge: backs sovereign domestic model while distributing Claude for enterprise and government — SOC services for finance, manufacturing, and local government sectors.

entities.name: Fujitsu
entities.desc: Japan's largest IT services firm. **Dual frontier AI partnership (May 27, 2026):** Signed resale + integration agreements with both OpenAI (ChatGPT Enterprise, Codex) and Anthropic (Claude) — largest Japanese IT integrator now official dual-frontier AI distributor covering government ministries and enterprise. Sets the pattern for NEC, Hitachi, NTT to follow. **AI Foundation Model Consortium (Issue #17):** Confirmed equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. — brings government and enterprise customer distribution to the domestic model project. Also member of MHI + PFN + Fujitsu supply chain for defense/critical infrastructure AI.

entities.name: Sony AI
entities.desc: Sony Group AI subsidiary. Member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (10%+ equity). Research focus covers robotics, gaming AI, and imaging intelligence. Sony's hardware ecosystem (PlayStation, cameras, sensors) provides unique data sources for physical AI training.

entities.name: Preferred Networks (PFN)
entities.zh: プリファードネットワークス
entities.desc: Japan's leading deep learning AI startup. PLaMo foundation models, MN-Core AI processors, PFCP cloud platform. Engineers seconded to SoftBank physical AI JV (announced April 2026). **MHI + PFN Business Alliance (Issue #7, Jun 2, 2026):** Alliance signed with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries for joint development of AI for mission-critical machinery — social infrastructure + national security/defense. PFN contributes PLaMo models and MN-Core AI processors; MHI contributes aerospace, defense, and energy hardware. Policy framing: Japan-made AI for keizai anzenhoshō (経済安全保障, economic security) domains. Capital alliance with MHI targeted within FY2026 (by March 2027).

entities.name: NTT Research
entities.desc: Research arm of NTT Group (日本電信電話). Quantum and AI research; Rapidus investor in ¥267.6B funding round. NTT is Japan's national telecom incumbent — provides critical infrastructure for data center connectivity underpinning Japan's AI ambitions.

entities.name: Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co.
entities.zh: 日本AIファウンデーションモデル開発
entities.desc: SoftBank-led consortium to build Japan's sovereign foundation model. June 2026 round closing: 30+ companies evaluating; ~10 formal equity commitments. **Newly confirmed (Issue #17):** Fujitsu, Yaskawa Electric, Asahi Kasei joining. Core original investors: SoftBank, NEC, Sony, Honda (each >10% stake); MUFG, Nippon Steel, Kobe Steel (small stakes). NEDO funding: up to ¥1 trillion over 5 years from FY2026 (~$6.3B). Target: trillion-parameter model for physical AI (robotics, autonomous vehicles, factory automation) by 2027. Governance risk: 30+ member consortium with no single controlling shareholder — velocity vs. frontier model iteration cadence is primary execution risk. Preferred Networks (PFN) engineers seconded. Commercial deployment not before 2027–2028.

entities.name: Rapidus
entities.desc: Japan's state-backed 2nm logic semiconductor project. IPA Capital Round #3 completed June 5, 2026: ¥150B new capital from IPA (METI agency). Cumulative IPA capital: ¥274.95B. Total funding (all sources): ¥424.95B (IPA equity + ¥167.6B from 32 private co-investors including Canon, Fujitsu, NTT, SoftBank, Sony, Development Bank of Japan). Total government commitment estimate: ~¥2.35T across all instruments. Target: full-scale 2nm manufacturing by 2027 at IIM-1 fab, Chitose, Hokkaido. Key open risk: no external customer supply commitment disclosed — needs hyperscaler or sovereign AI anchor customer.

entities.name: TSMC JASM (Kumamoto)
entities.desc: TSMC-majority JV in Kumamoto, Kyushu. Partners: Sony Group, Toyota, Denso. JASM-1: 6–12nm, production ramping 2024. JASM-2: upgraded to 3nm (approved April 2026), $17B total investment, government covers ~50%. Production target: 2028. Positions Kyushu as Japan's high-end semiconductor cluster alongside Rapidus Hokkaido. Serves automotive AI chip demand (Toyota, Honda, Denso supply chain).

entities.name: Kioxia
entities.desc: Japan's leading NAND flash memory manufacturer. Yokkaichi + Kitakami (北上) fabs. Cost per wafer ~$2,000 vs ~$4,000 Samsung, ~$6,000 Micron/SK Hynix — structural advantage through BiCS9. UBS initiated with Buy at ¥79,000 target (May 2026). Entire 2026 NAND output sold out. Q2 operating profit projected ¥1.3T — above full-year FY2025 record. BiCS10 (332-layer) will equalize cost advantage; UBS calls it a 12–18-month trade window. VLSI June 14: MSA-CBA 1,000-layer NAND demonstration.

entities.name: Tokyo Electron (TEL)
entities.desc: Japan's largest semiconductor equipment maker. Critical supplier of etch, deposition, and cleaning equipment to TSMC, Samsung, Rapidus. Under pressure from US export controls on advanced tool categories. Key beneficiary of Japan's semiconductor manufacturing renaissance.

entities.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
entities.desc: World's largest silicon wafer producer; critical input to TSMC Kumamoto and Rapidus Hokkaido. Also Japan's leading PVC producer. Semiconductor wafer division provides ~70% of silicon wafers used by leading-edge foundries globally.

entities.name: Fanuc
entities.desc: Japan's largest industrial robot and CNC machine maker. May 2026: announced Google Gemini integration enabling natural-language factory control — all future Fanuc robots will be compatible with Google software. Consortium member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV. METI physical AI initiative beneficiary. Key robotics data contributor for Japan's sovereign 物理AI model.

entities.name: Yaskawa Electric
entities.desc: Top-3 industrial robot maker globally. **AI Foundation Consortium (Issue #17):** Confirmed equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. Strategic significance: Yaskawa's production-floor automation data feeds directly into foundation model training pipeline — validates 'physical AI' framing as structural, not marketing. Core factory automation and motion control product lines remain primary revenue.

entities.name: JAL × GMO Humanoid Trial (Haneda)
entities.zh: JAL × GMO AI＆ロボティクス
entities.desc: Japan Airlines and GMO AI & Robotics launched a two-year Unitree G1 humanoid robot trial at Haneda Airport in 2026 for baggage, cargo, and cabin operations. First cycle-time data from week of June 1. METI June liability guidelines will be the policy gate determining how quickly pilots convert into scaled commercial operations.

entities.name: Honda Motor
entities.desc: Founding member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (10%+ equity). First designated external deployer of the sovereign physical AI model. Long AI/robotics history (ASIMO humanoid). AI Foundation Model Consortium capital round closing June 2026. Woven City (Toyota JV) adjacent AI infrastructure investment.

entities.name: Nippon Steel
entities.desc: Japan's largest steelmaker. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV consortium (June 2026 capital round). Materials science data (steel properties, processing conditions) key training input for physical AI foundation model. Represents heavy industry capital backing Japan's sovereign AI ambitions.

entities.name: Asahi Kasei
entities.desc: Diversified Japanese chemical and materials conglomerate (TSE: 3407). **AI Foundation Consortium (Issue #17):** Confirmed equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. Materials and healthcare data assets are likely AI training contribution. Earlier covered in the context of industrial AI adoption (Issues #4, #5).

entities.name: MUFG (Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group)
entities.desc: Japan's largest bank. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (June 2026). Government-authorized to deploy dual AI cyber stack: Anthropic Claude Mythos + OpenAI G-5.5 in tandem. Part of FSA working group on AI-related cyber risks (36 entities, 15 critical infrastructure sectors). Each 25bp BOJ rate hike adds ~¥100–150B in annual net interest income across the three megabanks.

entities.name: Mizuho Financial Group
entities.zh: みずほフィナンシャルグループ
entities.desc: Japan's third-largest bank. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (June 2026). Government-authorized for dual Claude Mythos + OpenAI G-5.5 AI cyber stack. BOJ rate normalization is structurally bullish for NII expansion.

entities.name: SMBC (Sumitomo Mitsui Banking)
entities.desc: Japan's second-largest bank. Government-authorized for dual AI cyber stack alongside MUFG and Mizuho. FSA working group participant. BOJ rate hike of 25bp adds ~¥100–150B NII across the three megabanks.

entities.name: Bank of Japan (BOJ)
entities.desc: Japan's central bank. Governor: Kazuo Ueda (植田和男). Policy rate: 0.75% (held April 2026, 6–3 vote split). Raised FY2026 core CPI forecast to 2.8% from 1.9%. OIS pricing June 2026: 77% probability of 25bp hike to 1.00% at June 15–16 MPM. Three dissenters favoured immediate hike. OECD projects 2.0% by end-2027. JGB purchase commitment signal at June MPM is the key 'hawkish rates / dovish duration' watch.

entities.name: Ministry of Finance (MoF)
entities.desc: Japan's fiscal authority. Finance Minister: Satsuki Katayama. Authorized record ¥11.73T (~$74B) FX intervention (為替介入) April 28–May 27, 2026 — first since July 2024, surpassing prior monthly record. USD/JPY hit ¥155 then retraced to 159.3. Issued fresh verbal warnings June 2026. 300bp US-Japan rate gap drives structural yen carry trade pressure.

entities.name: METI (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry)
entities.desc: Japan's industrial policy ministry. Core AI infrastructure funder and semiconductor strategist. ¥1.23T AI/semiconductor budget envelope; ¥387.3B specifically for AI development. Backs Rapidus 2nm semiconductor project (~¥2.35T total government commitment). AI Promotion Act (AI推進法): enacted 2026, innovation-first, voluntary guidelines for most applications. **Genesis Mission (Issue #11, Jun 4–5, 2026):** Japan named first international partner in U.S. DOE Genesis Mission — $1B combined ($500M each) over 5 years; 12 U.S. national labs + 12 Japanese research institutions; quantum technology, nuclear fusion, biotechnology, materials AI, advanced manufacturing. MEXT co-sponsoring. **AI Basic Plan revision (Issue #22, Jun 20, 2026):** Draft revision released for public comment — adds enhanced international cooperation provisions and new cybersecurity plank on AI-enabled cyberattacks. Cabinet approval sought at early date; cybersecurity budget line likely to follow.

entities.name: NEDO
entities.zh: 新エネルギー・産業技術総合開発機構
entities.py: Shin'enerugī Sangyō Gijutsu Sōgō Kaihatsu Kikō
entities.desc: New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization. Executing Japan's ¥1T AI fund (FY2026–FY2031). Approved Rapidus FY2026 plan (PDK general release + chiplet pilot). Expected FY2026 budget allocation for Rapidus 2nm delayed from May, now due June week 1. Administers public-private designation for Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV.

entities.name: Digital Agency (デジタル庁)
entities.desc: Established 2021. Leads Japan's digital transformation. Government Gennai (ゲンナイ) generative AI platform launched nationwide May 2026 — government-wide AI deployment. **APPI Amendment (Issue #12, Jun 2026):** Personal Information Protection Act amendment passed lower house; removes individual consent requirement for AI training on medical histories and criminal records. Digital Minister Matsumoto Hisashi used 'AI colony' (AIの植民地) framing — data deregulation as national sovereignty issue. Bill in upper house debate; must clear before parliament rises July 2026. No civil-remedy mechanism — key risk. Primary beneficiaries if passes: healthcare AI, insurance underwriting, enterprise NLP.

entities.name: FSA (Financial Services Agency)
entities.desc: Japan's financial regulator. Launched public-private working group on AI-related cyber risks: 36 entities across 15 critical infrastructure sectors. Authorized Japan's three megabanks (MUFG, SMBC, Mizuho) to deploy dual AI cyber stack (Claude Mythos + OpenAI G-5.5). AI cyber governance framework in development.

entities.name: SB OAI Japan GK
entities.zh: SBオープンエーアイジャパン
entities.desc: SoftBank-OpenAI joint venture, established November 2025. **Patching as a Service (launched June 17, 2026):** AI-powered enterprise vulnerability assessment and remediation. Phase 1 target: Japan's top 3,000 companies, focusing on critical infrastructure (airports, power grids, public transit). Technology: OpenAI's specialized cybersecurity models for vulnerability identification; advisory only (not automated code deployment). 50 dedicated security specialists at launch; target 1,000 personnel. Also operates Sarashina API service (launched Nov 2025). Positioned for METI government procurement contracts alongside commercial enterprise revenue. First revenue signal expected in SoftBank August 2026 quarterly earnings.

entities.name: PKSHA Technology
entities.desc: Tokyo-based AI software company (TSE: 3993). Bridges academic AI research and enterprise deployment in Japan. **Japan AI Index partnership (Issue #10, Jun 4, 2026):** Co-founding partner (with University of Tokyo + Anthropic) of the first Japan AI Index — fixed-point observation framework tracking AI's impact on employment, industries, economy, and education. First report October–November 2026; updates every 3–6 months. PKSHA's structural link to Japanese corporate sector makes it the enterprise deployment conduit for the index's findings. Creates the first credible, non-self-reported AI adoption data series for Japan.

entities.name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI)
entities.desc: Japan's largest defense and heavy industry manufacturer (TSE: 7011). Aerospace, defense, energy, and industrial systems. **PFN Business Alliance (Issue #7, Jun 2, 2026):** Alliance signed with Preferred Networks for joint development of AI for mission-critical machinery — social infrastructure + national security/defense. MHI contributes aerospace/defense/energy hardware + system integration expertise; PFN contributes PLaMo foundation models and MN-Core AI processors. Use cases: autonomous situational assessment, predictive maintenance, rapid crisis response in high-reliability environments. Policy framing: keizai anzenhoshō (経済安全保障, economic security) — defense customers prefer domestic supply chains. Capital alliance targeted within FY2026 (by March 2027). ITO corporate strategy framework guiding integration.
